text: Two classes measure stomatal density. Both have the same mean, but Class A has a much larger standard deviation. Which interpretation is best?

A larger standard deviation means the data are more tightly clustered.
Standard deviation tells how far the mean is from the true population mean.
Class A's measurements are more spread out around the mean.
explain: Standard deviation measures the spread of individual data points around the mean. A small standard deviation means the values are tightly clustered, while a large standard deviation means the values are more dispersed and less consistent.
choice_explanations: Incorrect. Mean and standard deviation describe different features of a data set; one can change without the other changing.
Incorrect. Larger standard deviation means more spread, not tighter clustering.
Incorrect. That idea is closer to uncertainty in the estimate of the mean, not to standard deviation.
Correct. This is exactly what standard deviation is intended to describe: variability around the mean.

explain: Standard deviation responds to how far data points lie from the mean. Outliers usually increase it, removing outliers usually decreases it, adding the same constant to all values leaves the spread unchanged, and multiplying all values scales the spread.
